queries: WITH r AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.location, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.location), k AS (SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY location ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_ratio IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_ratio DESC) AS rnk FROM r) SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, rnk AS rank FROM k WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY location, rnk, event_id;

responses.sql: WITH r AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.location, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.location), k AS (SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY location ORDER BY CASE WHEN avg_ratio IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END, avg_ratio DESC) AS rnk FROM r) SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, rnk AS rank FROM k WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY location, rnk, event_id;

assumptions.assumption: All events are included, via LEFT JOIN. Events with no budget lines, or only lines with amount = 0, get a NULL ratio and rank last in their location.
Budget lines with amount = 0 are skipped in the average, because the ratio is undefined for them (NULLIF gives NULL and AVG ignores NULLs).
The top 3 means rank <= 3, so tied events can give more than 3 rows per location. Events in the same location, including NULL locations, are ranked together.

assumptions.assumption: Events with no budget lines, or only lines with amount 0 (division yields NULL and is ignored by AVG), are kept with a NULL ratio and rank last within their location.
Top 3 means rank <= 3 using RANK, so ties at the cutoff can return more than 3 events per location. Events with a NULL location form their own group.

responses.sql: WITH ev AS (SELECT e.event_id, e.location, AVG((b.spent - b.amount) * 1.0 / NULLIF(b.amount, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM event e LEFT JOIN budget b ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id GROUP BY e.event_id, e.location), ranked AS (SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY location ORDER BY avg_ratio IS NULL, avg_ratio DESC) AS rnk FROM ev) SELECT event_id, location, avg_ratio, rnk AS rank FROM ranked WHERE rnk <= 3 ORDER BY location, rnk, event_id;

assumptions.assumption: All events are kept, including those with no budget lines. Their ratio is NULL and they rank after events that have a ratio.
A budget line with amount = 0 has no defined ratio. NULLIF turns it into NULL, and AVG ignores it. An event whose lines all have zero amount gets a NULL ratio.
Events with a NULL location are grouped together as one location.
Rank uses RANK(), so tied events share a rank and the next rank is skipped. Top 3 means rank <= 3, which can return more than 3 events per location when there are ties.
